source.title: Fine-Tuning Lowers Safety and Disrupts Evaluation Consistency
source.authors: Kathleen C. Fraser; Hillary Dawkins; Isar Nejadgholi; S. Kiritchenko

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether benign fine-tuning changes harmful-request fulfillment, using different models and the SORRY-Bench evaluation; also varies generation temperature. It does not test harmful-example fine-tuning or response-position KL.
record.gate_note: The paper reports other work's findings in its background, but those are not this study's results. Toxicity measurements concern the toxicity of non-refusal responses, not the refusal or fulfillment rate, so they are recorded under fits_no_version. The paper's fine-tuning and temperature results are shown mainly in figures; values not stated in the text are recorded as figure only.
record.test_reason: Fine-tunes Llama-3.2-1B and Mistral-7B-v0.3 on Qi et al.'s safety-filtered Dolly and Alpaca, plus GPT-4o-mini via the OpenAI interface. Harmful-request fulfillment is measured on SORRY-Bench over 5 seeds and checkpoints. It also compares generation temperature 0 vs 0.7. This is a different evaluator and different models aimed at the V2 question; the temperature comparison bears weakly on V4's decoding part.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also stress that fine-tuning 'not only degrades safety, but also disrupts evaluation consistency'. The self-generated-data result leads them to attribute degradation to the content/format of the fine-tuning data, not fine-tuning mechanics. They read the GPT-4o-mini decrease as provider safeguards, not as evidence that fine-tuning is safe.
record.recipe_differences: Tests benign instruction fine-tuning, including the Dolly and Alpaca versions used in earlier work, but uses Llama-3.2-1B and Mistral-7B-v0.3 and evaluates with SORRY-Bench. It adds repeated seeds and generation-temperature comparisons; the GPT-4o-mini fine-tuning method is unspecified.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported harmfulness depends on generation temperature for Llama-based models but shows no discernible temperature effect for Mistral-based models. Fine-tuning seed causes variance; dataset content and model also affect results. The authors report larger spread for fine-tuned models and substantial variability in repeated sampling.

fits_no_version.finding: Among non-refusals to hate-speech prompts, Dolly fine-tuning raises mean and maximum toxicity and variance for Mistral. Mean toxicity changes little for Llama. GPT-4o-mini fine-tunes produce some toxic outputs not seen in base.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning changes the severity of harmful compliance, separately from the fulfillment rate.

record.problems: The authors describe the study as preliminary and test only two relatively small open-source models plus a closed-source model. Much of the relevant numeric evidence is presented in plots rather than stated as values in the text. The SORRY-Bench evaluator's reported agreement with human annotations is 81% (Cohen's kappa), from its original evaluation. GPT-4o-mini's fine-tuning process is opaque, and its benchmark run omits 10 political-belief prompts.
record.rows_left_out: The study reports many checkpoint-level and repeated-measurement plot points. Separate epoch-by-epoch values are not extracted because the relevant values are figure-only and the text gives no exact scores for them; the retained rows capture the explicitly described comparisons and outcomes.

untested.parts: No harmful-example fine-tuning; adversarial fine-tuning appears only in cited background.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
Prefilling, adversarial suffixes, and decoding changes beyond temperature 0 vs 0.7 (no higher temperatures or other sampling settings).
The self-generated-data experiment addresses why fine-tuning degrades safety, not why alignment is shallow.
Other benign datasets, dataset sizes, and larger or clearly safety-tuned open models.

missing.what: Repeatability of benchmark on a single model at T=0.7: spread is larger for fine-tuned than base models. This concerns measurement reliability, not a version, but qualifies how V2 effect sizes should be read.

record.verdict_notes: All V2/V4 values are figure-only; the only stated number is the 0.73 vs 0.82 seed spread (Llama, Dolly, epoch 4, T=0.7). A key caveat for the open-model rows: the linked HF repos are base (non-instruct) models despite the text calling them instruction-tuned. If base models were used, the V2 'safety-trained' premise is not met. Not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests Dolly and Alpaca on the reported models, but not other benign datasets, data sizes, or model families beyond those described.
Per-token KL divergence and response-position concentration.
Prefilled compliant openings and adversarial suffixes; decoding changes other than generation temperature.
Whether safety is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
Whether the training objective or data produces safety shallowness.
Training to deepen safety across response tokens and whether it remains effective.
